questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an approach for measuring unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly Status Approach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monthly Status Approach **is NOT an approach for **measuring unemployment** in India.
 
• **Methods/measures for assessing unemployment:**
 
 
• **Usual status unemployment: **This method estimates the number of individuals who remained unemployed for a significant portion of the year. It typically provides the lowest estimates of unemployment.
 
• **Current weekly status: **This measure evaluates unemployment based on a single week. An individual is classified as unemployed if they were unable to work for any duration during the survey week.
 
• **Current daily status: **Under this approach, individuals who were unable to secure employment on one or more days during the survey week are considered unemployed. The daily status method is often seen as a comprehensive measure of unemployment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The unemployment rate** is calculated by dividing the number of unemployed individuals by the total labour force.
 
• The labour force comprises both employed and unemployed individuals. Individuals who are neither employed nor actively seeking employment, such as students and those engaged in unpaid domestic work, are categorized as being out of the labour force.
 
• According to the International Labour Organisation (ILO), unemployment is defined as being without a job, being available to work, and actively searching for employment.

questions.question: In which of the following regions in India are there high-grade iron ore deposit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **High-grade iron ore **deposits are primarily found in **Northern Odisha in India**.
 
• Northern Odisha in India is renowned for its abundant reserves of high-grade iron ore deposits.
 
• These deposits are concentrated in regions such as Keonjhar, Sundargarh, and Mayurbhanj districts.
 
• The iron ore found in this area typically exhibits high iron content and relatively low impurities, making it suitable for various industrial applications, including steel production.
 
• The presence of these valuable deposits has contributed significantly to the economic development of the region and has made Odisha one of the leading iron ore producing states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron ore** is a mineral substance essential for producing metallic iron through heating processes, serving as the primary source of iron for the global steel and iron industries.
 
• It typically comprises iron oxides and can exhibit various colors such as dark gray, bright yellow, deep purple, or rusty red. Iron ore exists in several forms, including magnetite, hematite, goethite, limonite, or siderite, with each form varying in composition and properties.
 
• Most iron ore deposits are found within sedimentary rocks known as banded iron formations (BIFs), characterized by alternating layers of iron-rich minerals and fine-grained silica rock called chert.
 
• These formations represent significant reservoirs of iron ore globally and are crucial for sustaining the production of iron and steel worldwide.

questions.question: The deficiency of Vitamin A causes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**night blindness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The deficiency of Vitamin A causes **night blindness**.
 
• **Vitamin A deficiency** can stem from insufficient dietary intake, issues with fat absorption, or liver-related disorders.
 
• This deficiency can compromise immune function and the production of blood cells, leading to symptoms such as skin rashes and characteristic eye problems like xerophthalmia and night blindness.
 
• Diagnosis often relies on identifying these ocular manifestations alongside low levels of vitamin A in the body.
 
• Treatment typically involves oral supplementation of vitamin A, although in severe cases or when malabsorption is a factor, administration via injection may be necessary.
 
• Foods rich in preformed vitamin A include fish liver oils, liver, egg yolks, butter, and dairy products fortified with vitamin A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Beriberi **is a condition resulting from a deficiency of thiamine, also known as vitamin B1. The term "beriberi" originates from a Sinhalese word meaning "extreme weakness".
 
• **Scurvy** is a disorder caused by a significant deficiency of vitamin C in the diet. It is characterized by severe symptoms of vitamin C deficiency.
 
• **Rickets** is a condition characterized by the softening and weakening of bones in children, typically due to prolonged and severe deficiency of vitamin D.

questions.question: Krishnadeva Raya, the most famous ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuluva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishnadeva Raya (1471 - 1529)** belonged to the **Tuluva dynasty** and served as its third ruler, reigning from 1509 to 1529.
 
• Under his leadership, the Vijayanagara Empire, which encompassed four prominent dynasties - Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu - flourished.
 
• Krishnadeva Raya's literary work, 'Amuktamalyada', provides insights into his profound sense of justice and his dedication to the well-being of his subjects.
 
• He is revered as one of the most illustrious monarchs in Indian history.
 
• His reign saw remarkable military successes, as he asserted his dominance by triumphing over formidable adversaries such as the Sultans of Bijapur, Golconda, the Bahmani Sultanate, and the Gajapatis of Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Tuluva Dynasty,** the third ruling lineage of the Vijayanagara Empire, derives its lineage from Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a formidable warlord hailing from the Tulu-speaking region in the west.
 
• His son, Narasimha Nayaka, orchestrated the downfall of the feeble Narasimha Raya II, thus ending the reign of the Saluva dynasty.
 
• Subsequently, Narasimha Nayaka ascended to the Vijayanagara throne as Viranarasimha Raya, marking the ascendancy of the Tuluva dynasty.
 
• The dynasty reached its pinnacle under the reign of Krishnadevaraya, the second son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Aravidu Dynasty** marked the fourth and final Hindu lineage to govern the Vijayanagara Empire in South India. Its inception was led by Tirumala Deva Raya, with his brother Rama Raya serving as the adept regent during the twilight of the preceding dynasty.
 
• Originating from the Kalyani region of northern Karnataka in contemporary India, **the Saluva dynasty **rose to power as the second ruling lineage of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Founded in the 14th century by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, **the Sangama dynasty** emerged as the inaugural ruling dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. They hailed from the lineage of Bhavana Sangama, with roots tracing back to the Yadava heritage.

questions.question: In 2022, what time did Chahat Arora wrap up the 100 m breaststroke race at the FINA World Swimming Championships in Melbourne, Australia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 ∶13.13s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the **FINA World Swimming Championships 2022 **in **Melbourne, Australia,** Indian swimmer **Chahat Arora** made headlines by establishing a national record in the women’s **100-meter breaststroke **event. 
 
• Clocking in at **1 minute and 13.13 seconds, **Arora's performance showcased her prowess in the pool. 
 
• However, Lithuania’s Ruta Meilutyte surged ahead in the overall heats with a remarkable time of 1 minute and 3.81 seconds, outpacing Arora by 9.32 seconds. 
 
• South Africa's 19-year-old Lara Van Niekerk secured second place with a time of 1 minute and 3.93 seconds, while Lilly King from the USA claimed the third spot, finishing in 1 minute and 3.94 seconds. 
 
• Looking ahead, Arora is set to participate in the women’s 50-meter breaststroke event, while Siva Sridhar will represent India in the 100-meter individual medley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Federation Internationale de Natation (FINA) **serves as the regulatory authority for a range of aquatic sports, including swimming, diving, water polo, synchronized swimming, and open water swimming.
 
• Operating as an international non-governmental organization headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, FINA was established on July 19, 1908, in London by eight founding entities, including British Swimming, the Hungarian Swimming Association, and the Fédération Française de Natation.
 
• Affiliated with the Association of Summer Olympic International Federations, FINA holds recognition from the International Olympic Committee for its role in overseeing international competitions within aquatic sports disciplines.

questions.question: What is the full form of MEDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro Enterprise Development Programme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The initial phase of the **Micro-Enterprise Development Programme (MEDP), **spearheaded by the** Ministry of Industry (MOI)** and** financed by UNDP,** concentrated on ten districts.
 
• Building upon insights gleaned from this phase, the subsequent phase refined the program's beneficiary criteria by prioritizing a significant proportion of the ultra-poor and socially marginalized, while maintaining its goal of ensuring 70 percent female participation.
 
• This stage extended the program's reach to an additional ten districts, thanks to financial backing from the Department for International Development (DFID) and New Zealand AID (NZAID). In 2006, MEDEP's emphasis on forest-based micro-enterprises received a boost with support from AusAID.
 
• Midway through 2007, UNDP augmented its funding to implement enterprise development in six districts under the 'Quick Impact for Peace Support Initiative' (QIPSI), as part of its direct contribution to peacebuilding endeavors.
 
• The third phase of MEDEP (2008-2010) commenced in April 2008 to bolster the national program on micro-enterprise development within the Three Years Interim Plan (2008-2010), with funding from UNDP and AusAID, maintaining a continued emphasis on supporting micro-enterprise development.
 
• Overall, MEDEP's geographic footprint expanded to cover 36 districts and successfully fostered the emergence of 47,664 micro-entrepreneurs, with 68% being women, 25% Dalits, and 69% youth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The objective of the** Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Development Project (SMEDP) **is to facilitate the accelerated growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). 
 
• This initiative particularly focuses on SMEs situated in non-urban and rural regions, aiming to enhance their access to long- and medium-term credit. 
 
• **The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises,** a key ministry within the Government of India, serves as the central executive authority responsible for crafting and implementing regulations, policies, and legislation pertaining to micro, small, and medium enterprises across the country.

questions.question: Bhimsen Joshi belongs to which of the following classical music traditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirana Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi**, a Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana tradition, excelled in the khayal form and gained fame for his renditions of devotional music.
 
• He toured Afghanistan, Italy, France, Canada, and the USA between 1964 and 1982, becoming the first Indian musician advertised on posters in New York City.
 
• Joshi organized the Sawai Gandharva Music Festival annually in homage to his guru and received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1998 and the Bharat Ratna in 2009.
 
• He played a key role in annually organizing the Sawai Gandharva Music Festival as a tribute to his guru, Sawai Gandharva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Kirana Gharana** is among the Indian classical khyal gharanas, focusing primarily on the intonation of notes (swara). In this style, precision in tuning and expression of individual notes (swaras) is paramount. 
 
• The Kirana Gayaki emphasizes that the swaras of the raga are not merely points in the scale but independent entities capable of expansive musical development. 
 
• Emotional pukars, or calls, in the higher octaves enrich the musical journey. Additionally, the gharana is distinguished by the intricate and ornate utilization of sargam taan, introduced by Abdul Karim Khan under the influence of Carnatic classical music. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Delhi or Dilli Gharana**, known as the oldest tabla discipleship tradition, was established by Sidhar Khan Dhadi in the early 18th Century.
 
• **The Banaras Gharana, **characterized by its robust sound, is renowned for its tabla players' ability to perform both powerfully and delicately.
 
• **The Jaipur Gharana **represents the ancient Hindu style of Kathak dance, which evolved not from one family or location but from numerous families of Kathak dancers throughout Rajasthan.

questions.question:
While travelling on a train, one of the travellers started speaking against the Indian freedom struggle and its noble ideals of.

Which of the following Articles mentions the fundamental duties in relation to such circumstances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A (b)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51-A (b) of the Indian Constitution** delineates a fundamental duty incumbent upon every citizen to uphold and abide by the lofty principles that served as the inspiration behind the nation's struggle for independence.
 
• Article 51 of the Indian Constitution is among the Directive Principles of State Policy, grounded in Liberal-Intellectual principles.
 
• It focuses on the promotion of international peace and security.
 
• The state is mandated to:
 
 
• Promote international peace and security.
 
• Maintain just and honorable relations between nations.
 
• Foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organized peoples with one another.
 
• Encourage the settlement of international disputes through arbitration. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 51A(c)** of the Constitution of India mandates that each citizen has the responsibility to safeguard and preserve the nation's unity, integrity, and sovereignty.
 
• **Article 51A(a) **stipulates that citizens are obliged to adhere to the Constitution, honor its principles and institutions, as well as show respect to the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• **Article 51A(d) **asserts that citizens are duty-bound to protect the country and contribute to national service when required. These provisions were incorporated into the Constitution through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

questions.question:
In India, credit creation is done by:

A) Ministry of Finance

B) Reserve Bank of India

C) Commercial Banks
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India,** commercial banks** play a crucial role in credit creation, while the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **regulates this process through various mechanisms such as the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), repo rate, and open market operations.
 
• Commercial banks generate credit by purchasing securities and extending loans, with the currency thus generated termed as credit money.
 
• Additionally, the RBI oversees the clearing of cheques among commercial banks and facilitates inter-bank fund transfers.
 
• Commercial banks are able to facilitate loans by leveraging the deposits acquired from the public. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Credit creation, **also referred to as "deposit creation," is the process wherein a country's money supply expands by utilizing a portion of customers' deposits to extend loans to businesses and individuals.
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), **India's central bank and regulatory authority, oversees the regulation of the Indian banking system. It operates under the ownership of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, and is tasked with controlling, issuing, and managing the supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• **The Ministry of Finance,** a department within the Government of India, focuses on managing the economy of India and functions as the Treasury. Its responsibilities encompass taxation, financial legislation, oversight of financial institutions, management of capital markets, administration of central and state finances, and formulation of the Union Budget.

questions.question: Who among the following devoted his life to the upliftment of widows and established the Widow Remarriage Association in 1893?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DK Karve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhondo Keshav Karve (1858 - 1962)** founded the **Widow Remarriage Association** in 1893.
 
• Also known as Maharshi Karve, he was a notable social reformer and educator advocating for women's education and the remarriage of Hindu widows.
 
• In 1893, Karve himself married a widow named Godubai, who had been widowed at the age of eight.
 
• Three years later, in 1896, he established the Hindu Widows Home to provide support for widows to sustain themselves.
 
• His contributions extended further with the founding of India's first women's university, S.N.D.T. Women's University, in 1916.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Annie Besant,** a British socialist, theosophist, freemason, women's rights advocate, Home Rule activist, educationist, and supporter of Indian nationalism, championed the causes of Irish and Indian self-rule. In 1917, she made history as the first female president of the Indian National Congress.
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen**, a Hindu philosopher and social reformer, sought to blend Christian theology with Hindu thought.
 
• **Behramji Merwanji Malabari JP, **an Indian poet, publicist, author, and social reformer, is renowned for his fervent advocacy for women's rights protection and his efforts against child marriage.

questions.question: In diffraction of white light by a prism, which colour of light from VIBGYOR will be bent most?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When white light travels through a prism, **violet light** bends the most, while red light bends the least.
 
• This occurs because violet light possesses the shortest wavelength among the seven colors in white light, while red light has the longest.
 
• **The dispersion of light,** which separates white light into its constituent colors, is responsible for this phenomenon.
 
• The refractive index of the medium is highest for violet light and lowest for red light. Refraction occurs as light enters the prism at an angle, with the degree of deviation varying based on wavelength. Consequently, different colors deviate at distinct angles, resulting in their separation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Violet light**, with the shortest wavelength among the seven constituent colors of light, experiences the greatest deviation, while red light, with the longest wavelength, undergoes the least. 
 
• Thus, the order of colors, commonly remembered as **VIBGYOR (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red),** reflects this sequence based on their respective wavelengths and degrees of deviation.

questions.question: Name the campaign launched by the Madhya Pradesh government on the occasion of National Girl Child Day on January 24, 2021, under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme.

The correct answer is __**PANKH Abhiyan**__.

questions.question: Lotia is a regional music form of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lotia** is a **traditional folk music genre** originating from **Rajasthan, India**.
 
• It finds its cultural expression through the voices of peasants as they toil in the fields, particularly during the Lotia festival, which typically occurs in the Chaitra month of the Hindi calendar.
 
• Thematically, Lotia revolves around the significance of water. During the festival, women participate by carrying lotas (vessels used for fetching water) and kalash (vessels symbolizing auspiciousness in water-filling rituals) filled with water sourced from ponds and wells.
 
• These vessels are adorned with vibrant flowers before being brought home, adding to the festive ambiance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Rajasthan boasts a rich tapestry of regional folk music styles, each with its own unique characteristics and cultural significance:
 
 
• **Maand:** Regarded as one of the most refined forms of folk music in Rajasthan, Maand has its origins in the royal courts where it was performed to honor the Rajput monarchs. It narrates tales of valor and sacrifice associated with Rajasthan's warriors.
 
• Panihari: This genre of music revolves around the theme of water, featuring songs that often depict the unexpected encounters of lovers amidst its lyrical narratives.
 
• **Kurjaa, Pipli, Rattan Rano, Mumal, Ghughri, Kevda: **These are among the many folk songs originating from the Marwar region, each carrying its own distinctive melodies and stories reflective of the local culture and traditions.
 
• **Kamad, Bhopey, Langas, Mirasi, Kalawant: **These represent some of the prominent musician castes hailing from the Eastern Plain region of Rajasthan. Each caste brings forth its own musical traditions, contributing to the diverse and vibrant landscape of Rajasthani folk music.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE with respect to simple model of the circular flow of economy?

i. The aggregate consumption is more than the aggregate expenditure.

ii. There is government intervention.

iii. There are no trade activities with the rest of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The basic circular flow model of the economy **operates without government intervention.
 
• This model illustrates the interconnected flow of money, goods, and services among economic participants.
 
• It serves as the foundation for national accounting and macroeconomics.
 
• Additional details about the **circular flow model** include:
 
 
• It delineates the overall structure of the economy, depicting exchanges between households and firms through both the factor and product markets.
 
• Households contribute land, labor, and capital to firms.
 
• Households purchase goods and services from firms in the product market.
 
• Firms compensate households for the resources they supply, which constitute factors of production.
 
• In reality, the model becomes more intricate with the inclusion of two additional elements: government involvement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Various circular flow models exist, each tracking a different number of sectors. 
 
• The following sectors could be incorporated into a circular flow model. Typically, each sector is denoted by a capital letter, often associated with GDP calculation methods. 
 
• Governments determine their gross national income by monitoring all injections into and withdrawals from the circular flow of income. When leaks match injections, the circular flow of income for a nation is deemed balanced.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian classical dancers was the recipient of the Padma Vibhushan award of 2003?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonal Mansingh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sonal Mansingh** is a prominent figure in Indian classical dance, specializing in Bharatanatyam and Odissi styles.
 
• Not only is she a highly respected dancer and Guru, but she has also been nominated by the President of India to serve as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Mansingh's contributions to the field have been recognized with prestigious awards, including the **Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2003.**
 
• Her illustrious dancing career began in 1962, with her arangetram in Mumbai, and in 1977, she founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi.
 
• In 2003, she received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, becoming only the second woman dancer in the country to be honoured in this manner after Balasaraswati.
 
• Mansingh's accolades continued with the Kalidas Samman from the Madhya Pradesh government in 2006.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Saswati Sen** was honored with a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2004 for her contributions to the field. 
 
• **Elam Endira Devi **was recognized with the Padma Shri award for her excellence in Manipuri classical dance. 
 
• **Birju Maharaj,** received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honor, in 1986, in recognition of his exceptional and distinguished service.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Established on January 2, 1954, the **Padma Vibhushan **is bestowed without discrimination of race, occupation, position, or gender.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is bestowed for exceptional and distinguished service, the Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of high order, and the Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field. These prestigious awards are announced annually on Republic Day.

questions.question: The Physical Quality of Life Index does NOT include which of the following indicators?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender development index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index** does NOT include Gender development index.
 
• **The Gender Development Index (GDI) **is a metric crafted to assess gender equality. 
 
• It, along with the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM), was introduced in the 1995 Human Development Report by the United Nations Development Program. 
 
• These measures were devised to imbue the Human Development Index (HDI) with a gender-sensitive perspective. The GDI was the initial outcome of this effort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) **seeks to gauge a country's well-being by averaging three equally weighted statistics: basic literacy rate at age 15, infant mortality, and life expectancy at age one.
 
• Developed in the mid-1970s by M.D. Morris for the Overseas Development Council, emerged from dissatisfaction with using Gross National Product (GNP) alone as a development indicator.
 
• Morris aimed to capture various aspects of development, including health, education, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• While PQLI offers an improvement, it faces challenges inherent in quantifying quality of life. Critics point out the overlap between infant mortality and life expectancy as a limitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The level of physical quality **of life is often seen as indicative of a country's economic development.
 
• A country with a higher physical quality of life is typically considered more developed than one with a lower quality.
 
• This assessment is based on three key standards: the extent of education, life expectancy, and infant mortality rate.

questions.question: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra is the cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra **are annual festivals observed by the **Dimasa tribe**.
 
• These socio-religious events are held before the commencement of new agricultural activities.
 
• The Rabha tribe celebrates the Baikho festival during the spring season to honor and seek blessings from the goddess of wealth, 'Baikho'.
 
• During this festival, the village headman, known as the 'Kunang', conducts rituals to appease the family deity by closing the village gate on the day of worship.
 
• Subsequently, on the same night, the community participates in the 'Harni Gabra' ceremony, dedicated to worshipping the presiding deity for the well-being and protection of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The major festivals celebrated in Assam are Bihu, Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baikho, Rongker, Rajini Gabra Harni Gabra, Bohaggiyo Bishu, Ambubashi Mela and Jonbill Mela and so on.
 
• The people of Assam also celebrate Holi, Durga Puja, Diwali, Swaraswati Puja, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja, Idd, Muharram, Me-Dam-Me-Phi, the birth and death anniversaries of Vaishnava Saints Srimanta Sankardev and Madhabdev.
 
• The tribals of Assam have their own colourful festivals like the Kherai Puja of the Bodos, the Baikhu and Pharkantis of the Rabhas, Ali-ai-ligang and Parag of the Mishing tribe, the Sagra-misawa wansawa and laghun of the Tiwas.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi?

__
 
• In February 2022, **Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit **made history as the **first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) in Delhi**, appointed by the Ministry of Education.

• Currently serving as the Vice Chancellor of Savitribai Phule University in Maharashtra, she brings a wealth of experience, having also served on prestigious bodies such as the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), in addition to being a Visitor's nominee to central universities. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru University,** a renowned public research institution located in Delhi, India, was established in 1969 through an act of parliament.

• The bill for its establishment was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 1 September 1965 by the then-Minister of Education, M. C. Chagla.

questions.question: What numerical scale was introduced in 1932 that determined the electronegativity of fluorine to be 4.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pauling scale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity,** a concept pioneered by **Linus Pauling in 1932,** measures an atom's ability within a molecule to attract electrons towards itself. It's described as "the power of an atom in a molecule to attract electrons to itself."
 
• On the Pauling scale, fluorine is set as the benchmark with an electronegativity of 3.98, and other elements are gauged relative to this value.
 
• Essentially, an atom's electronegativity indicates its tendency to pull electron density towards itself when forming bonds.
 
• Higher electronegativity signifies a stronger pull on electrons during bonding.
 
• Atomic number and atomic radius largely influence an atom's electronegativity.
 
• Across the periodic table, electronegativity generally increases from left to right and from bottom to top.
 
• Consequently, fluorine stands as the most electronegative element, while francium exhibits the least electronegativity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Allred-Rochow Electronegativity **method quantifies the electrostatic force resulting from the effective nuclear charge acting on the valence electrons of an atom.
 
• Mulliken's scale of electronegativity defines electronegativity as an inherent characteristic of an element, solely contingent on the valence state of the atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity** is the measure of an atom's ability to attract shared electrons in a covalent bond. A higher electronegativity value indicates a stronger attraction for the shared electrons. 
 
• This property follows a predictable trend across the periodic table: electronegativity generally increases from bottom to top within groups and from left to right across periods. 
 
• Consequently, fluorine holds the title of the most electronegative element, whereas francium ranks among the least electronegative.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution?

options.text: A loosening of traditional bonds or hereditary relationships between farmers or landowners and agricultural workers.
The rise of a class of 'free' wage labourers.
A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain).
There was an increase in the use of agricultural labour as cultivation became more intensive.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A shift from payment in cash** to payment in kind (grain) is NOT one of the impacts of the **green revolution**.
 
• **Payment-in-kind (PIK)** involves utilizing a commodity or service as compensation rather than cash.
 
• Additionally, it pertains to a financial instrument that provides interest or dividends to bondholders, note holders, or preferred stockholders through the issuance of additional securities or equity instead of cash.
 
• PIK securities are appealing to companies that wish to avoid cash expenditures and are frequently employed in leveraged buyouts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Green Revolution** denotes a historical period spanning from the 1940s to the 1960s, characterized by the development of high-yielding varieties of crops, notably wheat and rice, aimed at boosting food production.
 
• Its primary objective was to mitigate poverty and malnutrition by enhancing crop yields.
 
• The Green Revolution embraced innovative farming techniques and the introduction of new crop varieties, including: 
 
 
• High-yielding variety seeds
 
• Mechanized farm tools
 
• Irrigation facilities
 
• Pesticides
 
• Fertilizers
 
 
 
• Norman Borlaug is acclaimed as the **"Father of the Green Revolution."**
 
• In 1970, he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his efforts in pioneering the development of High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) of wheat.

questions.question: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in a Water Cycle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The hydration** step is NOT involved in a Water Cycle.
 
• **Hydration** involves replenishing the **body fluids** that are lost through sweating, exhaling, and waste elimination.
 
• Typically, the body loses and requires to replacement of approximately 2-3 quarts of water each day.
 
• Fortunately, many of the foods we consume are predominantly made up of water. Examples of such foods include leafy greens, as well as most fruits and vegetables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The water cycle,** also referred to as the hydrologic cycle or hydrological cycle, illustrates the perpetual movement of water across the Earth's surface, in the atmosphere, and beneath it.
 
• Throughout this cycle, water undergoes transitions between different states, while the total quantity of water particles remains constant.
 
• These state changes encompass processes such as evaporation, melting, freezing, sublimation, condensation, and deposition, all of which necessitate the input or release of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Condensation** represents the transformation of water vapor in the atmosphere into liquid water, contrasting with the process of evaporation. This step is pivotal in the water cycle as it leads to the formation of clouds.
 
• Above 0 degrees Celsius, water vapor condenses into water droplets. However, this condensation doesn't occur spontaneously; it relies on the presence of dust or other impurities. Water vapor adheres to the surface of these particles, eventually forming droplets. As these droplets coalesce, they precipitate out of clouds and onto the ground below, a phenomenon known as **precipitation or rainfall**.
 
• The sun serves as the primary energy source, driving much of the evaporation observed on Earth. **Evaporation** typically occurs when water molecules on the surface of bodies of water become energized and ascend into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Great Indian Desert?

options.text: Bounded to the west by the Aravali
Lies to the southeast of the Aravali
Lies to the northwest of the Aravali
Bounded to the south by the Aravali

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lies to the northwest of the Aravali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Thar Desert,** also referred to as the Great Indian Desert,** lies to the northwest of the Aravalli Range**, a mountain range extending from **Delhi to Gujarat **in northwest India.
 
• It comprises an undulating sandy plain adorned with sand dunes, serving as a natural demarcation between **India and Pakistan**.
 
• Acting as a barrier, the Aravalli Range obstructs moisture-laden winds from reaching the Thar Desert, resulting in arid conditions due to the rain shadow effect caused by the range.
 
• Ranked as the world's 18th-largest desert and the 9th-largest hot subtropical desert, the Thar Desert spans an area of 200,000 square kilometers (77,000 square miles) across India and Pakistan.
 
• Approximately 85% of the desert falls within India's borders, with the remaining 15% located in Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **The northeastern region** of the Thar Desert is situated amidst the Aravalli Hills, extending** towards Punjab and Haryana in the north,** reaching the Great Rann of Kutch along the coastline, and stretching towards the alluvial plains of the Indus River in the west and northwest.
 
• A considerable portion of the desert landscape is characterized by expansive, shifting sand dunes that accumulate sediments from the adjacent alluvial plains and coastline.
 
• These sand dunes exhibit high mobility, driven by the powerful winds that intensify annually before the arrival of the monsoon season.
 
• Within the desert, the Luni River stands as the sole watercourse.
